items.stem: A toy car is rolled across four floors. On which floor will it stop the soonest?

explain.why: A smooth surface has little friction, so the car goes further.
Ice has very little friction, so the car goes a long way.
A polished surface is smooth, so the car goes further than on carpet.

solution: A rough surface has more friction, so the car loses speed and stops sooner.

items.stem: A box is sliding to the right across a floor. In which direction does friction act on the box?
options: To the right, the same way as the motion
To the left, against the motion

explain.why: Friction does not help the box slide. It acts against the motion.
Friction acts along the surface, not upwards.
Gravity acts downwards. Friction acts along the surface against the motion.

solution: Friction always acts opposite to the way an object moves or tries to move.

items.stem: Why do running shoes have grooves on their soles?
options: To reduce friction so the runner can slide
To make the shoes lighter in the air
To increase friction so the runner does not slip
To make the shoes look nicer

explain.why: Grooves grip the ground. They increase friction.
Grooves are for grip, not for lightness.
The grooves have a job: they stop slipping.

solution: Grooves grip the ground. More friction means the shoe does not slip.

items.stem: Why is oil put on the chain of a bicycle?
options: To increase friction between the metal parts
To reduce friction between the metal parts
To make the chain stick to the wheel

explain.why: Oil makes surfaces slippery, so there is less friction.
Oil does not make the chain heavy.
Oil makes parts slide past each other more easily.

solution: Oil makes the surfaces slippery. Friction goes down and the chain moves more easily.

items.stem: Mei pushes a box along a smooth floor, then along a rough carpet with the same push. On which surface does the box move the shorter distance after she lets go?
options: It moves the same distance on both
It does not move on either surface

explain.why: A smooth floor has less friction, so the box goes further.
The two surfaces have different amounts of friction.
The push makes the box move on both surfaces.

solution: More friction on the carpet makes the box stop sooner.

items.stem: Which of the following ways will reduce the friction when moving a heavy box?

explain.why: A rougher floor means more friction.
Sand makes the floor rougher, so there is more friction.
Rubber grips the floor, so there is more friction.

solution: Wheels roll instead of rubbing, so there is much less friction.

items.stem: Which of these activities needs friction?
options: Walking on a path without slipping
Pushing a toy car on a smooth table

explain.why: A slide works best with little friction.
Skating needs little friction.
A car moves further when there is little friction.

solution: Friction between the shoe and the ground stops us from slipping when we walk.

items.stem: A pencil eraser gets smaller as it rubs against paper. Which force makes the eraser wear away?

explain.why: An eraser is not a magnet.
Gravity pulls the eraser down. Rubbing causes the wear.
There is no spring involved.

solution: Rubbing against paper causes friction, which wears the eraser away.

items.stem: A spring is hung from a stand. Gina replaces a 100 g mass by a 200 g mass. What happens to the spring?
options: It becomes shorter and then longer

explain.why: A bigger mass pulls harder, so the spring stretches more.
A greater load stretches a spring more.
The spring only stretches more when the load is bigger.

solution: A bigger load pulls the spring more, so it is longer.

items.stem: Which instrument is used to measure the size of a force?

explain.why: A measuring cylinder measures volume.
A thermometer measures temperature.
A stopwatch measures time.

solution: A spring balance stretches by an amount that shows the size of the force.

items.stem: A stretched spring is let go and goes back to its first length. Which force makes it do this?

explain.why: A spring is not a magnet.
Gravity pulls down, not along the spring.
Friction needs surfaces that rub.

solution: A stretched spring pulls back because of elastic spring force.

items.stem: Which of these things makes use of a spring?
options: A pen that clicks to push the tip out
A ball rolling down a ramp
A bar of soap sliding on a tray

explain.why: This works by magnetic force.
This works by gravity.
This involves friction.

solution: The clicking pen has a spring inside that pushes back.

items.stem: A spring is 10 cm long with no load. It is 14 cm long with a 100 g load. How much did the spring stretch?

explain.why: 14 cm is the new length. The stretch is the change.
10 cm is the first length.
Do not add. The stretch is 14 cm minus 10 cm.

solution: Stretch = new length - first length = 14 - 10 = 4 cm.

items.stem: A 50 g mass stretches a spring by 2 cm. How much will the same spring stretch with a 100 g mass?

explain.why: A bigger load stretches it more.
A bigger load stretches the spring more, not less.
Twice the load gives twice the stretch, which is 4 cm.

solution: The stretch is in proportion to the load, so twice the load makes twice the stretch: 4 cm.

items.stem: Which load will stretch the same spring the most?

explain.why: 20 g is the smallest load, so it stretches the spring the least.
A bigger load, 80 g, stretches the spring more.
A bigger load, 80 g, stretches the spring more.

solution: The bigger the load, the more the spring stretches.

items.stem: The weight of an object is the pull of which force on it?
options: The magnetic force of the Earth
The gravitational force of the Earth
The frictional force of the floor
The elastic force of the ground

explain.why: Not all objects are magnetic, but all have weight.
Friction does not give an object weight.
Elastic force is not what weight is.

solution: Weight is the pull of the Earth's gravity on an object.

items.stem: In which unit is weight measured?

explain.why: Kilogram is a unit of mass.
Metre is a unit of length.
Second is a unit of time.

solution: Weight is a force, so it is measured in newtons.

items.stem: What can be used to measure the weight of a bag?

explain.why: A ruler measures length.
A thermometer measures temperature.
A measuring cylinder measures volume.

solution: Hang the bag on a spring balance. The reading is its weight.

items.stem: Which of these objects has the greatest weight?

explain.why: A pencil is very light.
A rubber band is very light.
A paper clip is very light.

solution: The more matter an object has, the more the Earth pulls on it.

items.stem: In which direction does the force that gives an object its weight act?
options: Downwards, towards the centre of the Earth
In the same direction as the object moves

explain.why: Gravity pulls things towards the Earth.
Gravity does not pull sideways.
Gravity always pulls down, whichever way the object moves.

solution: Weight is the pull of gravity, which is towards the Earth.

items.stem: An apple is cut into two equal halves. What is the weight of one half, compared with the whole apple?
options: It is half the weight of the whole apple
It is the same as the whole apple
It is twice the weight of the whole apple

explain.why: Half the apple has half the matter, so half the weight.
Half an apple cannot weigh more than a whole one.
Every object has weight.

solution: Half the apple has half as much matter, so the Earth pulls with half the force.

items.stem: A mango is hung from a spring balance and the spring stretches. What makes the spring stretch?
options: The magnetic force on the mango
The elastic force of the spring

explain.why: A mango is not a magnet.
Air friction is very small.
The spring's own force pulls back. It does not make it stretch.

solution: Gravity pulls the mango down. This weight pulls the spring and stretches it.

items.stem: Does a feather have weight?
options: No, because it is too light
No, because it floats in the air
Yes, because gravity pulls on it

explain.why: Gravity pulls on light things too.
It falls slowly, but gravity still pulls it.
Weight comes from gravity, not friction.

solution: All objects have weight, even light ones, because gravity pulls on them.

items.stem: A boy rubs his hands together quickly and they get warm. Which force causes this?

explain.why: Gravity does not warm the hands.
Hands are not magnets.
There is no spring.

solution: Rubbing surfaces produce friction, which makes heat.

items.stem: A boy wants his toy car to roll as far as possible across the floor. Which floor should he use?
options: A floor covered with a rough mat

explain.why: Sand is rough, so there is a lot of friction.
A rough mat has a lot of friction.
Sandpaper has a lot of friction.

solution: A smooth floor has the least friction, so the car goes furthest.

items.stem: A toy car rolls down the same ramp onto four different surfaces. The table shows how far it moved on each. Which surface has the least friction?

explain.why: The car went 85 cm on tiles, less far than on the plastic sheet.
The car went only 40 cm on carpet.
The car went the shortest distance on the rubber mat, so it has the most friction.

solution: The car went furthest (110 cm) on the plastic sheet, so that surface has the least friction.

explain.why: On tiles the car went 85 cm. It lost speed slowly.
The car went 40 cm on carpet, further than on the rubber mat.
The car went furthest on the plastic sheet, so it lost speed slowest there.

solution: The car went the shortest distance (25 cm) on the rubber mat, so friction is greatest there.

Q and S differ in height and car size.
R and S differ in the surface and in the car, so it is not a fair test.

P and Q have the same ramp height and the same car, with different surfaces.

Q and S differ in height and in the size of the car.

options: It will be more than 45 cm
It will be less than 45 cm

explain.why: A smooth sheet has less friction than carpet, so the car goes further.
The surface is different, so the friction is different.
The car still rolls down the ramp.

solution: The plastic sheet is smoother than carpet. There is less friction, so the car goes further.

explain.why: The smallest reading (1 N) shows the least friction, which is the glass.
The reading on wood (3 N) is smaller than on sandpaper.
The reading on cloth (5 N) is smaller than on sandpaper.

Which of the following statements about friction are correct?
A: Friction acts when two surfaces rub against each other.
B: Friction acts in the same direction as the motion.
C: Rough surfaces have more friction than smooth surfaces.
D: Friction can never be useful.

explain.why: B is wrong. Friction acts against the motion.
Both are wrong.
D is wrong. Friction stops us from slipping when we walk.

solution: A and C are correct.
B is wrong: friction acts against the motion. D is wrong: friction is useful for grip.

C: A stretched spring stays stretched for ever.
D: A spring has no force when it is stretched.

explain.why: C is wrong. A spring returns to its length when the load is removed.
D is wrong. A stretched spring pulls back.
Both are wrong.

solution: A and B are correct.
C and D are wrong because a stretched spring pulls back and returns to its length.

Both are wrong.
D is wrong. All objects have weight.

solution: A and C are correct.
Weight is in newtons (not grams), and every object has weight.

A: Putting oil on moving metal parts.
B: Adding sand to a slippery path.
C: Using wheels instead of sliding.
D: Wearing shoes with deep grooves.

explain.why: B increases friction by making the path rough.
Both B and D increase friction.
D increases friction because the grooves grip.

solution: Oil and wheels reduce friction.
Sand and grooves increase friction.

items.stem: In an experiment on how the surface affects the distance a car travels, which is the variable that is changed?

explain.why: The ramp height should be kept the same.
This is what is measured.
The same car should be used each time.

solution: The experimenter changes the surface and keeps the car and height the same.

items.stem: In the same experiment, which is the variable that is measured?

explain.why: This is the variable that is changed.
This should be kept the same.
This should be kept the same.

solution: The distance the car moves is what is measured for each surface.

items.stem: The bar graph shows how far a toy car moved on four surfaces. Which statement is correct?
options: The car moved furthest on the ice
The car moved furthest on the carpet
The car moved the same distance on all of them
The car moved the shortest distance on the ice

explain.why: The carpet bar is the shortest.
The bars have different heights.
The ice bar is the tallest.

solution: The tallest bar is for ice, so the car moved furthest there.

items.stem: A 50 g mass stretches a spring by 2 cm. The same spring is stretched by a 175 g mass. If the stretch is in proportion to the load, how much will it stretch?

explain.why: 6 cm is the stretch with 150 g.
8 cm is the stretch with 200 g.
50 g gives 2 cm, so 175 g gives 3.5 times as much: 7 cm.

solution: 175 g is 3.5 times 50 g, so the stretch is 3.5 x 2 = 7 cm.

items.stem: A bag hangs from a spring balance and the reading is 6 N. What does the reading tell us?
options: The bag has a mass of 6 N
The spring pushes the bag down with 6 N
The Earth pulls the bag down with a force of 6 N
Friction on the bag is 6 N

explain.why: Mass is not measured in newtons.
The spring pulls up. The bag's weight pulls down.
Nothing is rubbing against the bag.

solution: The reading shows the weight of the bag, which is the pull of gravity on it.

items.stem: Ali pushes a book along a table and it stops as soon as he lets go. When he puts a few pencils under the book, it slides further. Why?
options: The pencils make the book heavier on the table
The pencils roll, so friction is less
The pencils push the book forward

explain.why: Pencils do not make the book heavier. They reduce friction.
Pencils do not push. They roll.
Rolling pencils reduce friction.

solution: Rolling has much less friction than sliding. So the book goes further.

items.stem: Two identical springs P and Q hang with different loads. P has a 100 g mass and Q has a 50 g mass. Which statement is correct?
options: P is longer than Q because it has the bigger load
Q is longer than P because it has the smaller load
P and Q are the same length
P is shorter than Q because it is heavier

explain.why: The bigger load stretches a spring more.
The loads are different.
A heavier load makes the spring longer, not shorter.

solution: The spring with the bigger load stretches more, so P is longer.

items.stem: Siti rolls a car down a ramp onto four surfaces. The table shows how far it travelled. Which conclusion is supported?
options: The car travelled furthest on the plastic sheet, so that has the least friction
The heavier the surface, the further the car travels
The car travels furthest on the surface with the most friction
Tiles have more friction than the rubber mat

explain.why: The weight of the surface was not tested.
More friction makes the car go a shorter distance.
The car went further on tiles (85 cm) than on the rubber mat (25 cm), so tiles have less friction.

solution: Plastic sheet: 110 cm, the furthest. So it has the least friction.
Rubber mat has the most friction.

items.stem: The table shows the length of a spring for different loads. The spring is 24 cm long with an unknown load. What is the load?

explain.why: 300 g would make the spring 22 cm long.
400 g would make the spring 26 cm long.
250 g would make the spring 20 cm long.

solution: Each 50 g adds 2 cm. From 10 cm to 24 cm is 14 cm.

items.stem: A spring is 12 cm long with no load. A 100 g load makes it 16 cm and a 200 g load makes it 20 cm. What is its length with a 350 g load, if it keeps stretching in the same way?

explain.why: This is the length with 250 g.
This is the length with 300 g.
The length is not 350 g divided by anything. Add the stretch (14 cm) to 12 cm.

solution: The stretch is 4 cm for each 100 g.
350 g stretches it 14 cm, so the length is 12 + 14 = 26 cm.

items.stem: A spring was stretched by a very heavy load. When the load was removed, the spring did not go back to its first length. What is the most likely reason?
options: The spring was not hung from a stand
The spring was stretched too much
The spring was too short at the start

explain.why: A stand has nothing to do with it.
A light load does not damage a spring.
A short spring is not damaged by length alone.

solution: A spring that is stretched too far is damaged and cannot go back to its first length.

items.stem: A man has a mass of 60 kg on Earth. On the Moon, gravity is weaker. Which statement is correct about the man on the Moon?
options: His weight is less than on Earth but his mass is the same
His weight and his mass are both less than on Earth
His weight is the same as on Earth but his mass is less
His weight and his mass are both the same as on Earth

explain.why: The amount of matter in him does not change. Only the pull of gravity does.
Weaker gravity gives less weight. His mass is unchanged.
Gravity on the Moon is weaker, so his weight is less.

solution: Weight depends on the pull of gravity. The Moon's pull is weaker.
Mass is the amount of matter, which stays the same.

items.stem: A spring balance shows 12 N for a bag on Earth. The same bag is taken to the Moon and weighed on the same spring balance. What will the reading be?

explain.why: The Moon's gravity is weaker, so the pull is smaller.
The pull is different on the Moon.
The Moon has gravity, so the bag still has weight.

solution: The Moon pulls less than the Earth.
So the spring stretches less and the reading is lower.

items.stem: On a wet road, a car takes a longer distance to stop than on a dry road. What is the best explanation?
options: Water increases friction between the tyres and the road
The wet road makes the car heavier
Water between the tyres and the road reduces friction
The tyres become smooth when they are wet

explain.why: Water makes the road slippery. Friction decreases.
The weight of the car does not change.
The tyres stay the same. The water is on the road.

solution: Water acts like oil. Less friction means the brakes stop the car less quickly.

items.stem: A skater glides far across smooth ice after one push. A skater pushed once on a rough floor stops quickly. Which statement explains why?
options: Ice has more friction so the skater keeps moving
Ice has less friction so the skater loses speed slowly
The rough floor has no friction
There is no friction on ice or on the rough floor

explain.why: More friction would stop the skater faster.
Rough floors have a lot of friction.
Friction acts on both. It is just much smaller on ice.

solution: Less friction means the skater slows down slowly and goes far.

items.stem: Mei pushes the same box with the same push on a rough floor and on a smooth floor. Which statement is correct?
options: The box travels further on the smooth floor because there is less friction
The box travels further on the rough floor because there is more friction
The box travels the same distance because the push is the same
The box travels further on the rough floor because the box is heavier there

explain.why: More friction stops the box sooner.
Different friction gives different distances.
The box weighs the same on both floors.

solution: Less friction on the smooth floor means the box slows down more slowly and goes further.

items.stem: A block is pulled across a table with a spring balance at a steady speed. The reading on cloth is 5 N. The same block is pulled on glass. What is the reading likely to be?

explain.why: Glass is smoother than cloth, so there is less friction.
The surfaces have different friction.
Some friction still acts on glass, so a small pull is needed.

solution: Glass has less friction than cloth, so a smaller pull is needed.

items.stem:
Which of the following statements about friction are correct?
A: It makes moving objects slow down.
B: It produces heat when surfaces rub.
C: It is bigger on a smooth surface than a rough one.
D: It acts only when objects are moving.

explain.why: C is wrong. A smooth surface has less friction.
D is wrong. Friction can act on a still object that is being pushed.
Both are wrong.

solution: Friction slows moving objects and makes heat when surfaces rub.
It is smaller on smooth surfaces.

items.stem:
Which of the following statements about the weight of an object are correct?
A: It is the pull of the Earth on the object.
B: It is smaller on the Moon than on Earth.
C: It is the same as the amount of matter in the object.
D: It acts upwards.

explain.why: C is wrong. The amount of matter is mass, not weight.
D is wrong. Weight acts downwards.
Both are wrong.

solution: Weight is the pull of gravity, smaller on the Moon. It acts downwards.

items.stem: Three tests use a ramp and a toy car. The ramp heights and distances moved on carpet are: 10 cm, 30 cm; 20 cm, 55 cm; 30 cm, 80 cm. Which conclusion is correct?
options: The higher the ramp, the further the car moves
The lower the ramp, the further the car moves
The height of the ramp has no effect
The car moves further on a rough surface

explain.why: The 30 cm ramp gave the longest distance.
The distance changes with the height.
The surface was not changed in these tests.

solution: The distance goes up as the height goes up: 30, 55, 80 cm.

items.stem: Ali's results for a ramp experiment do not show a clear pattern. He used a different toy car for each surface. What should he do to make his test fair?
options: Use a different ramp for each surface
Release the cars from different heights
Use the same toy car for every surface

explain.why: This would add another variable.
The height should be the same for every surface.
One measurement is not reliable. Repeating helps.

solution: Only the surface should change. The car, ramp and height must stay the same.

items.stem: Mei compares two springs P and Q to see which stretches more. What must she keep the same?
options: The number of coils in the springs
The load and the first length of the springs

explain.why: The springs are different, and that is what she is comparing.
These may be the difference being tested.
Colour does not affect stretching.

solution: To compare the springs, the load and first length should be the same.

items.stem: A heavy box is pushed along the floor. Which action will make the box stop sooner after a push?
options: Placing a rough mat under it

explain.why: Rollers reduce friction, so the box slides further.
Oil reduces friction.
Polished tiles have less friction than carpet.

solution: A rough mat increases friction, so the box stops sooner.

items.stem: Why do machines have oil between their moving metal parts?
options: It reduces friction and wear on the parts
It increases friction so that the parts stay in place

explain.why: Oil reduces friction.
The oil is a thin layer. It is not for weight.
Oil has no effect on magnetism.

solution: Oil keeps the metal parts from rubbing directly, so less friction, less heat and less wear.

items.stem: A block hangs from a spring balance and does not move. Which two forces act on the block?
options: Its weight downwards and friction upwards
Magnetic force downwards and the spring force upwards
Its weight upwards and the spring force downwards
Its weight downwards and the elastic spring force upwards

explain.why: There is no rubbing surface, so no friction.
A magnet is not involved. Gravity pulls down.
Weight acts down.

solution: Gravity pulls the block down.
The stretched spring pulls it up with the same size of force, so it stays still.

items.stem: The graph shows how the length of a spring changes with load. What is the first length of the spring, with no load?

explain.why: A spring has length even with no load.
12 cm is the length with 100 g.
2 cm is the stretch for 50 g, not the first length.

solution: With no load (0 g), the line starts at 8 cm.

explain.why: 14 cm is the length with 150 g. The spring gains 2 cm per 50 g.
The spring gains 2 cm per 50 g, so only 16 cm.
200 g is the load, not the length.

solution: The length goes up by 2 cm for each 50 g.
At 150 g it is 14 cm, so at 200 g it is 16 cm.

items.stem: Two bags hang from separate spring balances. Bag X reads 8 N and bag Y reads 3 N. Which statement is correct?
options: The Earth pulls X with a bigger force than Y
Y is pulled by the Earth with a bigger force than X
The Earth pulls X and Y with the same force
X has less matter than Y

explain.why: The bigger reading means the bigger pull.
The readings are different.
The bigger weight means more matter, not less.

solution: The reading is the weight. The bigger reading (8 N) is the bigger pull of the Earth.

items.stem: A spring balance has a spring that stretches more for a heavier load. Why must the scale on a spring balance have equal spaces between marks?
options: The spring stretches more and more for each extra gram
The spring does not stretch at all
The marks are only there to make the scale look neat
A spring stretches equally for each equal extra load

explain.why: A spring stretches by equal amounts for equal extra loads.
A spring balance works because the spring stretches.
The spaces show forces. They are equal because of how the spring stretches.

solution: A spring stretches in equal steps for equal extra loads, so the scale can be marked evenly.

items.stem: A bag is taken from the Earth to the Moon. Which of the following would NOT change?
options: The pull of gravity on the bag
The amount of matter in the bag
The reading on a spring balance

explain.why: Weaker gravity on the Moon gives the bag less weight.
The Moon pulls less than the Earth.
The spring stretches less on the Moon.

solution: The amount of matter in the bag stays the same.
Weight, the pull of gravity and the spring balance reading are all smaller on the Moon.

items.stem: Which action makes it harder to slide a heavy cupboard across the floor?
options: Putting a wet cloth under the cupboard
Putting a thick rubber sheet under the cupboard
Putting small wheels on the cupboard

explain.why: Wetness reduces friction.
Oil makes it easier to slide.
Wheels reduce friction.

solution: A rubber sheet grips the floor, so friction is greater.

items.stem: A spring is stretched by 3 cm by a 60 g mass. By how much would two identical springs hung side by side share the 60 g mass?

explain.why: The load is shared, so each spring has only half of it.
The load is shared, so each stretches less.
Each spring still carries 30 g.

solution: Each spring carries 30 g, half the load, so it stretches half as much: 1.5 cm.
